purpose: Compare frozen, explainable machine judgments with later-revealed human technical review feedback. This known-failure supplement is not included in blind merge-outcome accuracy.

required: at least one non-bot human PR review
at least one explicit human technical feedback item
excluded: review text revealed before the machine lock

order: verify exact patch identity and expected path set
state the patch claim and caller-visible invariants
look for removed or silently ignored interface semantics
look for test coverage contraction or broad diagnostic suppression
run the smallest affected static, build, and runtime checks
search for a more central ownership point when the same fix is repeated across leaf modules
freeze accept-with-scope, revise, reject, or unresolved with explicit evidence and counterchecks
only then reveal reviewer feedback and compare concepts without rescoring

cases.claim: Move three kernel tests into the runtime test suite and add them to CI.
predeclared_questions: Are all moved tests still discoverable from their new paths?
Did the move preserve the previous case matrix and diagnostic visibility?
Does run_suite reference every moved file exactly once?
Do the affected test modules still parse and collect?

cases.claim: Add a block barrier before token threads consume shared local offsets.
predeclared_questions: Can every thread in the block reach the new barrier?
Does the barrier separate a shared-memory write phase from a read/atomic phase?
Does the exact affected kernel compile for SM80?
Do repeated adversarial routing cases match a CPU reference with and without the patch?

cases.claim: Compute DeepSeek router logits and routing probabilities in FP32.
predeclared_questions: Does FP32 routing improve or preserve numerical agreement?
Is the public renormalize argument still honored on every changed top-k path?
Are softmax and sigmoid paths covered?
Does changing gate parameter dtype preserve checkpoint loading and surrounding module contracts?
